items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: I liked his style in playing too. Very good. And I listened to his playing as much as much. I used to listen to him on Saturday night.

ctx.x: You mean from hearing him in person or from the records?

From, hearing him in person, both ways, you see. Yeah, I liked him better than all of them. And there was another one that was a sort of preference. I don't know if you heard of him. His name was Perez, Manuel Perez. Yeah, I liked his style in playing too. Very good. And I listened to his playing as much as much. I used to listen to him on Saturday night. My backyard and the backyard around the corner met like that. And they had, used to give a long party they called at the time. Never had no, and there was brass…

items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What kind of tunes do you think Man of Prayer was playing? ... [INTERVIEWEE] He was playing like, you mentioned the name, Scott Joplin and things of that sort, yeah.

ctx.x: Yeah. So somebody else, some other musician, would come along and copy and get the same music they got. See? So that would make them, they felt that we had, they would hear somebody else with music. Uh huh. You know, with the tunes there.
What kind of tunes do you think Man of Prayer was playing? Was he playing ragtime tunes?
He was playing like, you mentioned the name, Scott Joplin and things of that sort, yeah.
